analysis.title: "Long One Corner, Short Everything Else": Goldman Says The AI Unwind Is Rotation, Not Liquidation
key_insights: A CXMT-triggered memory selloff went global overnight: KOSPI -5.5%, Samsung -8%, SK Hynix -10%, Kioxia -13%, Nasdaq futures -70bps at one point while Russell futures were +30bps (per Goldman's TMT desk). SOXX is on track for a sixth straight down day.

Goldman EMEA delta-one head Rich Privorotsky (GS Basics) says the market got 'incredibly long one corner and effectively short everything else', and dispersion has flipped. SPX barely moved while semis underperformed and the broader market strengthened.

In Japan, five stocks account for the entire Nikkei decline (Nikkei roughly -1.5-2%) while TOPIX traded slightly up. Privorotsky reads this as an unwind of crowded positions, not indiscriminate selling.

The trigger was China's CXMT claiming a 4F² DRAM architecture breakthrough that would put it ahead of Samsung and Hynix despite US sanctions. Elon Musk added that 'RAM was a low margin commodity only 3 years ago.'

Goldman's Robert Quinn: Goldman's Memory and AI Semiconductor baskets fell 9.3% and 6.7% between Oct 5 and Oct 12. Nasdaq lost 1.3% against a 0.4% gain in the S&P. CFTC 'Other' gross longs in Nasdaq futures were at one-year highs on Oct 6, in notional terms and as a share of open interest.

Privorotsky had warned on Oct 12 that speculators were heavily short bonds and Russell and long Nasdaq, so the pain trade was clear. Bonds stabilized, bond vol compressed, gold found a bid, and equal weight and Russell outperformed.

Monday was the lowest-volume session of the year per Goldman's TMT desk. Goldman's S&P ex-AI basket finished +64bps and equal weight beat cap weight. The 10Y yield was down 4bps to 5.19% this morning. Long bond implied vol has given back nearly half its move.
Year-end P&L protection and thin liquidity make crowded exits violent. Privorotsky says there is less appetite to intermediate risk and last week was difficult for alpha.

Privorotsky's key risk view: locally AI positioning is problematic, but aggregate equity exposure remains incredibly low and nets are conservative. He calls it rotation rather than wholesale liquidation.

Privorotsky's playbook: Russell, equal weight and Europe should outperform while AI hardware digests its excesses. Financials could reinforce the rotation given a low bar after de-rating ahead of numbers. Hyperscalers are a cushion because they own scarce compute and inference demand is accelerating. The hardware leg struggles but the dip ultimately gets bought.
JPMorgan kicked off bank earnings with a surprise drop in FICC revenue. The stock was down 3.6% premarket before recovering on higher NII guidance. Goldman also missed on FICC.

Privorotsky says Hock Tan's comments comparing AI investors to gamblers were taken out of context. He says Broadcom and Intel reaffirmed strong demand for another 2-3 years, potentially through 2030. He calls LT ROI a legitimate question but hardly a revelation.

The Zerohedge author counters that Tan is arranging roughly $145 billion in chip financing for customers and Broadcom's 5Y CDS printed a record 136bp last week. JPMorgan and Goldman declined to underwrite a $3.7 billion GPU loan for Volta Infrastructure. The loan still drew more than $5 billion in orders from private credit, hedge funds and mutual funds (Bloomberg).

Privorotsky names the real risk as the ability to complete capacity and deliver power relative to expectations, which he says is fueling further de-rating in the capex vertical. He expects a choppy market while positioning clears, and says he is not sure much new has been learned beyond memory competition.

The Zerohedge author disagrees that the hardware dip gets bought, arguing the hyperscaler cushion depends on the buildout staying funded and funders are nervous. Upcoming catalysts: CPI tomorrow, ASML earnings tomorrow before the open, TSMC Thursday, SEMICON West capex, packaging and HBM headlines.

Goldman also missed on FICC revenue in its earnings.
Broadcom's 5Y CDS printed a record 136bp last week and CEO Hock Tan is arranging roughly $145 billion in chip financing for customers. This is the Zerohedge author's view, not Goldman's.
Samsung fell 8% and SK Hynix 10% in Korea after China's CXMT claimed a 4F² DRAM architecture breakthrough.
Kioxia fell 13% in Japan on the memory selloff. Advantest, Tokyo Electron and SoftBank were also under pressure.

sector_views.rationale: Privorotsky says the hardware leg struggles, caught between crowded positioning, Chinese competition and capex concerns, but expects the dip to ultimately be bought.
Privorotsky does not think hyperscalers go down much because they own scarce compute and inference demand is accelerating.
Privorotsky expects Russell to outperform while AI hardware digests its excesses, with speculators heavily short Russell.
Equal weight should outperform cap weight in the rotation.
Europe is expected to outperform while AI hardware digests its excesses.
Privorotsky says financials could reinforce the rotation with a low bar after de-rating ahead of numbers. The author notes JPM and GS both missed on FICC.

earnings_insights: JPMorgan Q3 earnings reported 10/13: FICC revenue dropped versus expectations (surprise miss). The stock fell 3.6% premarket before recovering on higher NII guidance. No EPS figure given in the report.
Goldman Sachs Q3 earnings reported 10/13: missed on FICC revenue. No EPS figure given in the report.
ASML reports 10/14 before the open and TSMC reports Thursday 10/15. Both are flagged as the next tests for the semiconductor rotation.

tension_points.bull_case: Privorotsky: aggregate equity exposure is incredibly low and nets are conservative, so this is rotation not liquidation. Hyperscalers own scarce compute, inference demand is accelerating, Broadcom and Intel reaffirmed demand for 2-3 years, and the hardware dip ultimately gets bought.
tension_points.bear_case: Zerohedge: the hyperscaler cushion assumes the buildout keeps getting funded, but Broadcom's 5Y CDS is at a record 136bp and JPMorgan and Goldman declined the $3.7B Volta loan. Low exposure also means little dry powder to defend the dip.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further AI financing stress or failed deals, and the ASML (10/14) and TSMC (10/15) earnings reports.
